text:
Connor O'Brien: Heads up: need to lock runtime-1.21 branch cut timing today. Main items: tiered batching feature flag default, and whether we’re backporting the streaming cadence hotfix. Goal is no surprises for Dedicated/Private.

Sahana Iyer: CI note: perf-canary is a bit noisy this week (2 flakes in the last 20 runs). If we cut the branch too early, we’ll be chasing flakes on the release branch.

Sofia Ivanova: For tiered batching: code is behind `batching_tier_defaults_enabled` (server-side flag). Default OFF unless explicitly set via config. We can keep it OFF in 1.21 and do staged enablement post-release.

Benji Okafor: Confirming: flag is in the rollout service, supports % by (model, region) targeting. If we ship 1.21 with the flag OFF, there’s no behavior change unless control-plane flips it.

Rafael Mendes: SRE preference: ship with flag OFF, enable only for beta cohort in 1-2 regions. Also want a clean rollback story: flip flag back + auto-rollback hooks on p95/p99 + timeout rate.

Connor O'Brien: +1. Proposed branch cut: Monday 10:00am PT. After that: only release-blocker fixes, no feature work.

Mateo Alvarez: Works. But we should decide on backport for the fast-tier streaming cadence fix (the decode prioritization tweak). That one is already in main and is low-risk.

Sofia Ivanova: You mean the fix that came out of the fast-tier regression? That’s in PR 18463. It only changes decode scheduling weights when streaming=true and tier=fast. I’d call it safe to backport.

Diego Santos: From deployment config angle: I’m worried about Private folks pinning runtime versions. If we don’t backport and they enable tiering later, they could hit the streaming issue. Backport seems prudent.

Sahana Iyer: If we backport, please don’t also pick up the scheduler refactor. Keep it surgical. The refactor touched too much and is more likely to trigger perf-canary flakes.

Connor O'Brien: Agreed. Backport policy for 1.21: only cherry-pick the minimal hotfix PR(s), no refactor.

release-bot: Reminder: runtime-1.21 branch cut draft scheduled for 2025-03-03 10:00 PT. Please add any release blockers to the tracking doc before cut.

Rafael Mendes: What are we calling “release blocker” here? For me:
- crash/OOM increase
- >5% p95 regression on default tier (standard/off) in core regions
- increased timeouts/cancellations
Anything else should wait.

Mateo Alvarez: That matches. Also if the new queue-delay metrics cause cardinality explosion or ingestion lag, that’s a blocker (we’ve been burned).

Sahana Iyer: Metrics look ok in staging, but I’ll run a quick scrape-size check today. If it’s fine, I’m comfortable with the current instrumentation shipping.

Connor O'Brien: Action items:
1) Sofia: confirm PR 18463 is cleanly cherry-pickable onto the release branch (no deps).
2) Benji: confirm flag name + default OFF in 1.21 manifests.
3) Sahana: confirm CI/perf-canary stability plan for release branch (rerun policy + flake labeling).
4) Rafael: paste rollback thresholds we should watch during the first flag ramp.

Sofia Ivanova: PR 18463 cherry-picks cleanly, only touches scheduler params and adds a regression test. No schema changes.

Benji Okafor: Flag details:
- Name: `batching_tier_defaults_enabled`
- Default: false
- Targeting dimensions: customer_id, model, region
- Max ramp step: 10% per 30 min (configurable)
I’ll make sure release notes mention “shipped behind flag; no default behavior change.”

Sahana Iyer: CI plan: release branch requires green unit + integration + perf-canary (2 retries allowed). If perf-canary fails twice, tag as flake vs real regression using the benchmark-lab diff report. I’ll be on point for the first 48h after branch cut.

Rafael Mendes: Rollback thresholds for initial ramp (beta only):
- p95 latency +10% vs baseline for the same (model, region, route)
- timeout rate +0.3% absolute (or >1.5x) over 30m window
- cancellation rate +0.5% absolute
- queue_delay_p95 > 2x baseline (watch but not immediate rollback unless paired with timeouts)
If any two trigger => auto-rollback flag to previous %.

Connor O'Brien: Great. Proposed decisions (unless objections by EOD):
- Cut runtime-1.21 branch Monday 10am PT.
- Ship tiered batching feature flag OFF by default.
- Backport only PR 18463 (streaming cadence fast-tier hotfix) to the release branch.
- No scheduler refactor backports.
React with :thumbsup: if good.

Mateo Alvarez: :thumbsup:

Sofia Ivanova: :thumbsup:

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup:

Benji Okafor: :thumbsup:

Sahana Iyer: :thumbsup: (and please do not merge anything else Friday afternoon :)

Connor O'Brien: Noted. I’ll start the backport PR once the branch is cut and tag reviewers. Also will update the release train checklist with the flag/rollback notes.
